after.proposed_name: diacylglyceryl lipoprotein intramolecular O-to-N acyltransferase activity
after.proposed_definition: Catalysis of intramolecular transfer of the sn-2 ester-linked acyl chain of the N-terminal S-diacylglyceryl-L-cysteine of a lipoprotein to its free alpha-amino group, yielding a lyso-form lipoprotein with one O-linked and one N-linked acyl chain.
after.justification: Direct purified-enzyme product analysis and NMR in PMID:34253723 resolve the sn-2 donor within the same substrate. The existing intramolecular acyltransferase genus is valid but does not encode this substrate, donor position, or lyso product. Total acyl-chain number remains two; this is not the intermolecular third-chain addition catalyzed by Lnt, Lnb, or LnsAB.

supported_by.supporting_text: These data prove that the acyl chain transferred by Lit comes from the sn-2 position of the DAG in the BLP substrate.

after.proposed_definition: Catalysis of intermolecular transfer of an acyl group to the free alpha-amino group of the N-terminal S-diacylglyceryl-L-cysteine of a lipoprotein, producing a triacylated lipoprotein.
after.justification: The acyltransferase genus is valid but does not identify the lipoprotein acceptor or terminal N-acylation reaction. Lnb-dependent reporter mass spectrometry and native B. thetaiotaomicron genetics establish the product chemistry in cells. The physiological acyl donor and purified-enzyme reaction remain unresolved, so this proposal deliberately does not require the phospholipid donor established for Lnt or LnsAB. BF9343_0945 reporter rescue in E. coli and BT_4364 native mutant/complementation are distinct assay scopes.

genes/ECOLI/lgt/lgt-ai-review.yaml.before: GO:0009898 explicitly includes proteins embedded in the cytoplasmic leaflet, so a polytopic topology does not refute this location. The 2008 pT7GT/BL21(DE3) inverted-vesicle extraction assay suggested peripheral association and acknowledged possible preparation/overexpression artifacts. Later direct topology shows seven spans and a cytoplasmic C terminus. Retain the sided-presence claim as a non-core spatial aspect, not as proof of native cytoplasmic catalysis or a soluble peripheral enzyme; the supported catalytic site is toward the membrane/periplasmic region and the core location remains plasma membrane.
genes/ECOLI/lgt/lgt-ai-review.yaml.after: The original PMID:18602442 study extracted activity from inverted membrane vesicles of pT7GT-overexpressing BL21(DE3), reporting approximately 95% water-extractable activity and acknowledging possible preparation or overexpression artifacts. PMID:22287519 subsequently established seven membrane spans and argued that the earlier soluble fraction could contain membrane-associated aggregates. GO:0009898 includes embedded proteins, so integral topology does not by itself refute cytoplasmic-leaflet presence. Conversely, a cytoplasmic C terminus alone does not resolve the original whole-protein localization interpretation. Keep the experimental row unresolved rather than treating either interpretation as a direct native sided-location assay. Plasma-membrane localization remains supported in the core.

genes/PSEPK/lspA/lspA-ai-review.yaml.before: LspA directly hydrolyzes the peptide bond before the lipid-modified cysteine. Proteolysis is therefore a true core process, not an overannotation merely because the enzyme recognizes a specialized substrate. Lipoprotein biosynthesis captures the pathway context separately. Obsolete GO:0006465 signal peptide processing is not introduced as a replacement.
genes/PSEPK/lspA/lspA-ai-review.yaml.after: LspA itself cleaves the signal peptide from diacylglyceryl-prolipoprotein. Refine the true but broad proteolysis annotation to GO:0016485 protein processing, an is_a descendant of GO:0006508. The target assignment is supported by curated UniProt function and family membership, with conserved LspA mechanism supported by PMID:26912896; this is not a native KT2440 biochemical assay. The same substrate-processing distinction applies to the ECOLI and BACSU ortholog reviews.

genes/PSEPK/lspA/lspA-ai-review.yaml.before: Signal-peptide removal is direct proteolytic work during lipoprotein maturation.
genes/PSEPK/lspA/lspA-ai-review.yaml.after: LspA proteolysis specifically processes a lipoprotein precursor.

after.proposed_definition: Catalysis of the phospholipid-dependent N-acylation of the N-terminal S-diacylglyceryl-L-cysteine of a bacterial lipoprotein.
after.justification: Reconstitution in PMID:42580408 establishes phospholipid-dependent terminal N-acylation by the compatible LnsA/LnsB complex, with preference for the sn-1 acyl chain of phosphatidylglycerol under the tested conditions. This substrate-specific proposal matches the Lnt activity proposal without asserting a shared mechanism or family. LnsA supplies the catalytic center but requires its compatible LnsB partner; no autonomous LnsA activity is asserted.
